infrastructure::conventions_resolve::par.docs: Front-matter codec seam: decodes one document's text into `ConventionFrontMatterDto`, and is the single enforcing site of AC-07's two decode conditions (YAML parse, `required_for` shape). Kept a `FreeFunction` (R2: no state, no dependency) and separate from the directory scan so that decode behaviour is testable from strings alone, and so a document defect cannot be raised by any other layer. Reuses the crate-internal front-matter block reader already used by provider-definition parsing rather than adding a second block scanner (design self-check 12). AC-06, AC-08.

infrastructure::conventions_resolve::sca.docs: Directory-scan seam: walks the convention tree read-only, builds a `ConventionDocumentPath` per file — which is where the path invariant is established rather than re-checked here — and hands each document's text to the codec. Single enforcing site of AC-07's unreadable-document condition. A `FreeFunction` (R2) and deliberately three seams apart from decoding and matching, so filesystem behaviour is testable without front-matter fixtures and neither neighbour can acquire a filesystem dependency. IN-05, AC-06.

infrastructure::template_conventions::li.docs: Tree-inventory seam: walks a tree's convention directory read-only and returns one `ConventionDocumentPath` per document, tree-relative so the exported tree and the overlay tree yield directly comparable identities rather than paths that must be normalised before comparison. Single enforcing site of all three `ConventionShippingCheckError` conditions. It reads no file contents and parses no front matter, which is what keeps a malformed document from turning a shipping question into a parse failure — and is why it does not reuse `scan_convention_requirements`, whose whole purpose is that decode. A `FreeFunction` (R2), separate from the set comparison for the same seam reason as the resolver's scan. IN-11, AC-18.

CapabilityIdField.docs: Deserializable serde-boundary mirror of one `required_for` element — the R9 mirror-type pattern, since the validated capability identifier is a serde-free usecase value. Keeping the wire value a distinct type is what lets the two AC-07 conditions it sits between stay separately observable: a non-string element fails as a serde shape error, an empty element fails at conversion, whereas a raw `String` would collapse both into one untyped parse failure. Its single field holds unvalidated wire text and is never exposed, so no caller can mistake it for a validated identifier. AC-06, AC-09.

ConventionFrontMatterDto.docs: Serde view of a convention document's YAML front matter, carrying only the optional `required_for` list of `CapabilityIdField` mirrors. Unknown keys are tolerated by design, because consumer documents own their own metadata and this codec has no business rejecting fields it does not read. Its `Default` value is also what a document with no front-matter block decodes to, so AC-08's two absent-metadata states share one representation and no caller has to distinguish them. `into_requirement` is the single enforcing site of AC-07's empty-identifier condition, placed on the DTO because that is where the unvalidated elements are held. AC-06.

FsConventionInventoryAdapter.docs: Filesystem implementation of `ConventionInventoryPort`, delegating to `list_convention_documents` (IN-11, AC-18). One adapter serves both sides of the comparison, so the two inventories cannot drift in walking rules. Kept as a stateless unit struct rather than folded into the free function it wraps — R2's trait-boundary exception, since the port is injected as a trait object and a free function cannot satisfy one; this mirrors the neighbouring `FsConventionRequirementAdapter` shape.

FsConventionRequirementAdapter.docs: Filesystem implementation of `ConventionRequirementPort`, delegating to `scan_convention_requirements` (IN-05, AC-06, AC-07). Kept as a stateless unit struct rather than folded into that free function — R2 would otherwise fold a zero-field single-method type away, but the port is injected as a trait object, which a free function cannot satisfy; this mirrors the existing `FsConventionsAdapter` shape.
